findings.title: Prologue: s0=self, s1=PLAYER work struct @0x800CFBF8, s2=distance, s4=±1024 cone, s3=±512 cone — and a THIRD cone call whose result is DEAD
findings.meaning: DELAY-SLOT ASSIGNMENT (this is the trap): `addu s4,v0,zero` @0x8010176C is the delay slot of the jal @0x80101768, so it captures the return of the FIRST call (half-angle 1024). `addu s3,v0,zero` @0x8010178C is the delay slot of the jal @0x80101788 and captures the SECOND call (half-angle 512). The THIRD call (half-angle 1300) returns into v0, which is immediately overwritten by `lbu v0,574(s0)` @0x80101790 — its result is never used, and FUN_80015614 has no stores, so this call is pure dead code. Port it as: s4 = cone_test(±1024), s3 = cone_test(±512), and either emit or omit the 1300 call (no observable effect). s2 = self+0x1F0 = distance to player (confirmed separately). s1 = 0x800CFBF8 = the PLAYER work struct (proved: the EXE passes exactly this pointer as a0 to the player per-frame routine 0x8003BFAC at `80025c5c: addiu a0,14864(s3)` / `80025c64: jal 0x8003bfac`, and s1+0x38 = 0x800CFC30 = the same X word loaded here as the bearing target).
openQuestions: Why the 1300-cone call exists at all (leftover from a removed test, or intentionally kept for cycle timing?) — no reader found.

verdict.why: Independently re-disassembled; every element of the claim reproduces. (1) INSTRUCTIONS: `dis 0x80101714 60 --bin EMZ0.BIN` matches the quoted listing exactly. (2) DELAY SLOTS verified at BYTE level via `bytes 0x80101768 40`: `80101768: 85 55 00 0c`=jal 0x80015614, slot `8010176c: 21 a0 40 00`=0x0040a021=addu rd=20(s4),rs=2(v0) -> s4 captures v0 entering call#2 = return of call#1 (a3=1024, set in slot `8010174c: 00 04 07 24`); `80101788: 85 55 00 0c`=jal, slot `8010178c: 21 98 40 00`=0x00409821=addu rd=19(s3),rs=2(v0) -> s3 = return of call#2 (a3=512 @`80101754: 00 02 07 24`). Claim's assignment is CORRECT. Downstream use independently corroborates: `801017f4: sll v0,s3,16` + `801017f8: bne v0,zero` and `80101864: sll v0,s4,16`. Deadness itself clean: `80101790: lbu v0,574(s0)` clobbers v0 with two fillers (80101794/80101798) before `8010179c: bne v0,zero`, so no R3000 load-delay hazard preserves R3. (5) PLAYER STRUCT: cited proof verified — `800257cc: lui s3,0x800d` / `800257d0: addiu s3,s3,-15896` -> s3=0x800CC1E8, so `80025c5c: addiu a0,s3,14864` = 0x800CC1E8+0x3A10 = 0x800CFBF8 passed to `80025c64: jal 0x8003bfac`. (The tool's inline `0x800d3a10` annotation on that line is a tool artifact computed off the lui base, not real s3.) Two extra corroborations the claim did not cite: `8010193c: addiu a1,s1,56` re-forms s1+0x38=0x800CFC30 (same word used as bearing target), and 0x8003bfac does `8003bff4: lbu v1,467(s0)` / `8003c008: sb v0,467(s0)` on that same pointer — the identical +467 field the zombie RMWs at `80101900`/`8010195c`/`80101968: sb v0,467(s1)`. (6) CONE SEMANTICS supported by actual code, not invented: FUN_80015614 reads `80015638: lh a0,56(s0)` (self X@+0x38), `8001563c: lh a1,64(s0)` (self Z@+0x40), `80015648: lhu v1,118(s0)` (yaw@+0x76), then `80015658: andi v1,v0,0xfff`, `80015664: sll v0,s1,1`, `80015668: slt v0,v1,v0`, `8001566c: bne v0,zero,0x80015684` delay `80015670: addu v0,zero,zero` -> 0 inside the +/-half cone, else +half (`8001567c: addu v0,s1,zero`) or -half (`80015680: subu v0,zero,s1`). verdict.correction: No refutation — claim stands as portable. Two calibration notes rather than errors. (a) The claim's justification for the dead 1300 call was UNDER-ARGUED: "FUN_80015614 has no stores" is insufficient, because purity requires the whole chain FUN_80015614 -> FUN_800154AC -> 0x8008d190. I verified all three are sp-store-only and COP2-free, so the conclusion survives; but the claim should cite that chain, especially since a genuine global store (`8008d270: sw ra,-9348(at)` -> 0x800ADB7C) sits only 0x14 bytes past 0x8008d190's `jr ra` at 0x8008d25c and belongs to a different function. Recommended port note: the 1300 call may be omitted safely — it touches no globals, no GTE regs, and no PRNG. (b) The label "PLAYER" for 0x800CFBF8 should be marked INFERRED (strongly corroborated), not PROVEN: the address arithmetic 0x800CC1E8+0x3A10=0x800CFBF8 is proven, and the shared +0x38/+0x40 position layout, the shared +467 byte field between 0x8003bfac and the zombie routine, and consistency with the established +0x1F0 distance-to-player all point to the player — but no symbol-level proof of the word "player" was produced, and the cited call site 0x80025c5c sits in an init-style routine (0x80025794) rather than a demonstrated per-frame path, so calling 0x8003BFAC "the player per-frame routine" is itself unproven framing.

findings.title: Helper FUN_80015614 / FUN_80015714 / FUN_80015758 semantics — polarity: 0 == INSIDE the cone
findings.meaning: FUN_80015614(ent, targetX, targetZ, half): d = (bearing(ent.x@+0x38, ent.z@+0x40 -> targetX,targetZ) - ent.yaw@+0x76 + half) & 0xFFF; returns 0 if d < 2*half (target INSIDE the ±half cone), else +half if d < 0x801, else -half (which side). So `s4 == 0` means "player within ±1024", `s3 == 0` means "player within ±512". FUN_80015714(ent, absAngle, half) is the same test but against an already-computed absolute angle instead of a bearing. FUN_80015758(pA, pB, angle, half) computes bearing(pA->pB) with x at +0 and z at +8 of each pointer, then returns `!(((bearing-angle+half)&0xFFF) < 2*half)` — note the trailing `xori v0,v0,0x1`: it returns 0 for INSIDE, 1 for OUTSIDE, the same polarity as the other two. Every caller in the decision handler branches with `bne v0,zero -> skip`, i.e. "skip unless inside". 4096 = 360°, so half=1024 is ±90°, 512 is ±45°, 256 is ±22.5°.

verdict.why:
The HEADLINE polarity (0 == INSIDE) is CONFIRMED and survives every attack I made — but the claim's caller-side generalization is FALSE, contradicted by a literal instruction, and it is exactly the kind of statement a porter would code against.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (re-disassembled myself, delay slots re-checked, bytes verified):

1. FUN_80015614 — semantics exactly as claimed.
   80015638: lh a0,56(s0)      ; ent +0x38
   8001563c: lh a1,64(s0)      ; ent +0x40
   80015640: jal 0x800154ac    ; delay 80015644: sra a3,a3,16
   80015648: lhu v1,118(s0)    ; +0x76
   80015650: subu v0,v0,v1
   80015654: addu v0,s1,v0
   80015658: andi v1,v0,0xfff
   80015664: sll v0,s1,1       ; 2*half
   80015668: slt v0,v1,v0
   8001566c: bne v0,zero,0x80015684
   80015670: addu v0,zero,zero  <-- DELAY SLOT, executes on BOTH paths; 0x80015684 is the epilogue (lw ra,24(sp)/jr ra). d<2*half => v0=0. So 0 == INSIDE. Delay-slot assignment in the claim is correct.
   80015678: bne v0,zero,0x80015684 / delay 8001567c: addu v0,s1,zero (=+half) / fallthrough 80015680: subu v0,zero,s1 (=-half). Correct.

2. FUN_80015714 — is a real function entry (8001570c: jr ra / 80015710: nop precede it) and matches: 80015714 lhu v0,118(a0); 80015734 slt v0,a1,v0; 80015738 bne v0,zero,0x80015750 with delay 8001573c addu v0,zero,zero. 0 == INSIDE.

3. FUN_80015758 — full listing confirms: 80015778 lh a0,0(v0) / 8001577c lh a1,8(v0) / 80015780 lh a2,0(v1) / 80015784 lh a3,8(v1) / 80015788 jal 0x800154ac (delay 8001578c sll s1,s1,16) / 8001579c subu v0,v0,s1 / 800157a8 addu v0,v0,s0 / 800157ac andi v0,v0,0xfff / 800157b0 sll s0,s0,1 / 800157b4 sltu v0,v0,s0 / 800157b8 xori v0,v0,0x1. 0 == INSIDE.

4. Independent corroboration the claim did not use: sibling FUN_80015558 runs the identical idiom and, when the test says INSIDE, executes 800155d8: j 0x800155f8 with delay slot 800155dc: sh v1,118(s1) — it SNAPS yaw(+0x76) to the bearing; otherwise 800155e0: subu v1,a1,s2 / 800155e8: sh v1,118(s1) (yaw -= half) or 800155ec-800155f4 (yaw += half). This proves both that +0x76 is the writable heading and that "d < 2*half" is the in-cone case.

5. 4096 = full circle is proven, not assumed: FUN_800154AC uses 800154b0 addiu v0,zero,1024 / 800154e8 addiu v0,zero,3072 / 80015534 addiu v0,zero,4096 / 80015538 addiu v0,zero,2048 / 80015540 andi v0,v0,0xfff.

6. s4/s3 binding is right (the tricky delay-slot capture): 80101748 jal 0x80015614 with delay 8010174c addiu a3,zero,1024; its v0 is captured at 8010176c addu s4,v0,zero, which is the DELAY SLOT of the NEXT jal (80101768) and therefore still holds call#1's result. Likewise 8010178c addu s3,v0,zero (delay slot of the jal at 80101788) holds the a3=512 call's result. Raw bytes verified: 80101774: 14 05 07 24 (addiu a3,zero,1300) ... 85 55 00 0c 21 98 40 00 (jal 0x80015614 / addu s3,v0,zero).

WHAT FAILS — the claim states: "Every caller in the decision handler branches with `bne v0,zero -> skip`, i.e. 'skip unless inside'." That is refuted twice in the very handler it describes (0x80101714):

   8010185c: sltiu v0,s2,0xdac
   80101860: beq v0,zero,0x801018a4
   80101864: sll v0,s4,16          <-- delay slot
   80101868: beq v0,zero,0x801018a8   <-- beq, NOT bne
   8010186c: sltiu v0,s2,0x9c4
   ...
   8010189c: addiu v0,zero,3073
   801018a0: sw v0,4(s0)

Raw bytes @0x80101860: 10 00 40 10 | 00 14 14 00 | 0f 00 40 10 | c4 09 42 2e = beq v0,zero,0x801018a4 / sll v0,s4,16 / beq v0,zero,0x801018a8 / sltiu v0,s2,0x9c4. Branch target 0x801018a8 is PAST the state-3073 store at 0x801018a0, so the action fires only when s4 != 0 — i.e. only when the player is OUTSIDE the +/-1024 cone. Same again at 801018ac: sll v0,s4,16 / 801018b0: beq v0,zero,0x801018e8 (skips the second 3073 store at 801018e4).

A porter following "skip unless inside" would invert both of these gates: the zombie would trigger sub_state 3073 while facing the player instead of while the player is off to the side. That is a real behavioral inversion, not a wording nit.

TWO FURTHER DEFECTS I FOUND (neither noticed by the claim):

A) A third helper call in that handler is DEAD. 80101788: jal 0x80015614 with a3=1300 (80101774: addiu a3,zero,1300); its return value is clobbered on the very next instruction, 80101790: lbu v0,574(s0) (bytes 3e 02 02 92). Nothing captures it. Any port that "faithfully" wires up a 1300-wide cone gate here is inventing a gate that does not exist.

B) "FUN_80015714 ... is the same test" / "the same polarity as the other two" hides a byte-level divergence: 80015668 and 80015734 use SIGNED slt, while 800157b4 uses UNSIGNED sltu. For half <= 0 the three functions disagree (signed: always OUTSIDE; unsigned: always INSIDE/0). Every caller I found passes positive halves (1024/512/1300/256), so it does not bite today, but the three must NOT be collapsed into one shared C helper.
verdict.correction:

 - FUN_80015614(ent, targetX, targetZ, half): d = (FUN_800154AC(ent.x@+0x38, ent.z@+0x40, targetX, targetZ) - ent.yaw@+0x76 + half) & 0xFFF @0x80015658; returns 0 if (signed) d < 2*half @0x80015668/0x8001566c+delay 0x80015670; else +half if d <u 0x801 @0x80015674/0x80015678+delay 0x8001567c; else -half @0x80015680.

REPLACE the caller sentence with the measured inventory for WALK decision @0x80101714 (s2 = lw 496(s0) = +0x1F0 distance @0x80101744):

 7. 0x801018b0 beq v0,zero,0x801018e8 on sll v0,s4,16 (0x801018ac) = require OUTSIDE +/-1024 (second 3073 path, DAT_800cfbf6 & 0x17, PRNG & 1 == 0 @0x801018d8/0x801018dc).
 8. 0x80101948 jal FUN_80015758(ent+0x38, other+0x38, yaw+256 (delay 0x8010194c), half=256) -> 0x80101950 bne v0,zero,0x8010196c = require INSIDE.
 9. 0x8010198c jal FUN_80015758(ent+0x38, other+0x38, yaw-256 (delay 0x80101990), half=256) -> 0x80101994 bne v0,zero,0x801019e8 = require INSIDE.
So: 4 gates require INSIDE (bne->skip), 2 gates require OUTSIDE (beq->skip), 1 call is dead. The rule is NOT "skip unless inside"; the polarity of the consumer branch must be read per call site.

STILL UNKNOWN (do not invent): which physical side +half vs -half denotes (left or right) — no call site consumes the sign, so it is unconstrained by anything I disassembled; the meaning of ent +0x1F8 (fed to FUN_80015714 @0x801017cc) beyond "an angle in the same frame as yaw, since it is subtracted from +0x76"; and the globals 0x800cfc30 / 0x800cfc38 (passed as targetX/targetZ, 8-byte stride matching the x/z layout) are only INFERRED to be the player position.

findings.title: s2 IS the distance to the player: +0x1F0 = SquareRoot0(dx²+dz²) vs 0x800CFBF8
findings.meaning: The lead's assumption is CONFIRMED. In the EXE's per-entity pre-dispatch pass, s2 = s3+14864 = 0x800CFBF8 (the player), and +0x1F0 (offset 496) is written with sqrt((self.x-player.x)² + (self.z-player.z)²) via 0x8008D2F4. Note `mflo a0` @0x800265C0 sits between the second `lw` pair and its `mult` — it harvests the FIRST multiply; the add of the two squares happens in the jal delay slot @0x800265D8. So s2 in the decision handler is an unsigned XZ-plane Euclidean distance in world units, compared against 3500 / 2500 / 2000 / 1200 / 1000 below.

verdict.why:
I independently re-derived every load-bearing element and could not break it.

VERIFIED VERBATIM: the block 0x800265a4-0x800265e0 disassembles exactly as quoted (the claim silently omits `nop`s at 0x800265ac and 0x800265c8, but its address column is transparent about the gaps and no semantics change).

DELAY SLOTS CHECKED BOTH WAYS: `800265d4: jal 0x8008d2f4` has delay slot `800265d8: addu a0,a0,v1`, so a0 = dx²+dz² at call time — as claimed. I also checked the inverse error: `800265e0: sw v0,496(s0)` is NOT in a delay slot, and the intervening `800265dc: lbu v1,8(s0)` writes v1, not v0, so v0 is still the SquareRoot0 return value. `mflo a0` @0x800265c0 does harvest the FIRST mult (issued @0x800265b4), and `mflo v1` @0x800265d0 harvests the second (@0x800265cc). No branches in the block to misassign.

s3 PROVEN (the claim asserted the arithmetic but never proved s3): function prologue at 0x80025794 (`addiu sp,sp,-80`) contains `800257cc: lui s3,0x800d` / `800257d0: addiu s3,s3,-15896` -> 0x800CC1E8. 0x800CC1E8 + 14864 = 0x800CFBF8. Confirmed.

0x8008D2F4 IS SquareRoot0 (PROVEN, not assumed): `.word 0x4884f000` = MTC2 a0,$30 (LZCS), `.word 0x4802f800` = MFC2 v0,$31 (LZCR), early-out `beq v0,at(32) -> return 0`, normalize by shift, `lh t5,-9332(t5)` from table 0x800adb8c, `srl v0,t5,12`. I decoded that table as Q12 halfwords: 4096, 4127, 4159, 4190, 4222... = sqrt(1+n/64)*4096. Matches the known BIOS 192-entry approximation.

ORDERING SUPPORTS "before the dispatch": `sw v0,496(s0)` @0x800265e0 precedes the per-type handler call `jalr v0` @0x800265f4 (table at s3+15476), inside the entity loop 0x80026570-0x80026608. So +0x1F0 is fresh when the zombie handler runs.

THE X/Z AXIS ASSIGNMENT — the claim's weakest link — is independently corroborated: the WALK decision handler loads absolutes 0x800CFC30 (@0x80101724) and 0x800CFC38 (@0x8010172c), which are exactly 0x800CFBF8+0x38 and 0x800CFBF8+0x40, the same two offsets used in the distance calc, and passes them into FUN_80015614, which reads self's `lh a0,56(s0)` / `lh a1,64(s0)` and calls the already-established bearing fn FUN_800154AC (with yaw at +0x76 via `lhu v1,118(s0)`). Same planar pair, +0x3C (Y) skipped. So "XZ-plane, vertical ignored" holds.

s2-IS-+0x1F0 PROVEN in the handler: `80101744: lw s2,496(s0)`.

ALL FIVE CONSTANTS EXIST, all as `sltiu` (genuinely unsigned) against s2: 0x7d0=2000 @0x801017fc and @0x801019c8; 0xdac=3500 @0x80101840 and @0x8010185c; 0x9c4=2500 @0x8010186c/84/98/a4; 0x4b0=1200 @0x801018f4; 0x3e8=1000 @0x801019fc. I initially could not find 1000 in the first 90 instructions and expected this to be the failure point, but it appears at 0x801019fc.

0x800CFBF8 = PLAYER is INFERRED (well-supported), not symbol-proven: it sits outside the entity list, gets a dedicated post-loop pass (`80026610: addiu s0,s3,14864` / `8002661c: sw s0,8520(s3)` then jal 0x8003bfac / 0x800355c4 / 0x8003567c / 0x80077600), and FUN_8003bfac (called with a0=0x800CFBF8) decrements field +467 (`8003bff4: lbu v1,467(s0)` ... `8003c008: sb v0,467(s0)`) — the same +467 the zombie reads from it at `8010181c: lbu v0,467(s1)`. Consistent, but the claim labels this PROVEN when it is a strong inference.
verdict.correction:
The mechanism is correct and portable as described. Three refinements the claim should carry into the port:

1. NOT exact Euclidean distance. The headline says SquareRoot0 but the MEANING text says "integer sqrt" / "Euclidean distance". 0x8008D2F4 is a GTE-LZC-normalize + 192-entry Q12 TABLE APPROXIMATION (table @0x800adb8c = 4096, 4127, 4159, 4190, ...; result `srl v0,t5,12` @0x8008d364). A port using floor(sqrt()) WILL diverge at threshold boundaries — and every one of the five thresholds is a strict unsigned `sltiu`, so a single-unit error flips a branch. Use the existing re15_squareroot0 equivalent, not libm.

2. Signed 32-bit overflow must be replicated. `mult v0,v0` @0x800265b4/0x800265cc is the SIGNED multiply and `addu a0,a0,v1` @0x800265d8 wraps at 32 bits. For large separations the sum can carry into the sign bit, after which LZCS/LZCR (`MTC2 a0,$30` / `MFC2 v0,$31`) take a different path. Do the arithmetic in int32 with wraparound; do not promote to int64.

3. "s2" is overloaded and the headline is literally wrong about its own snippet. In the quoted EXE code s2 is the PLAYER POINTER (`lw v1,56(s2)` / `lw v1,64(s2)` use it as a base). It is only in the decision handler at 0x80101714 that s2 becomes the distance VALUE (`80101744: lw s2,496(s0)`). The MEANING paragraph disambiguates correctly, but the headline "s2 IS the distance to the player" should be reworded to avoid a future reader mis-porting the EXE snippet.

Minor: label the "0x800CFBF8 = the player" step INFERRED rather than PROVEN. It is well-supported (dedicated non-list processing pass, shared +467 field with FUN_8003bfac, used as the bearing/distance reference for every entity) but no symbol or pad-input write to it was demonstrated.

findings.title: BLOCK A @0x801017A4 — the only EARLY-RETURN outcome: 'threat entity in front' lunge (0x0E01)
findings.meaning: Guard chain (all must hold): (1) self+0x23E == 0 (the bne @0x8010179C above, whose delay slot 0x801017A0 loads the 0xC0000000 mask); (2) self+0x1F4 & 0xC0000000 != 0; (3) (self+0x1F4 & 0x3FFFFFFF) < 2000; (4) FUN_80015714(self, self+0x1F8, 256) == 0, i.e. the angle stored in +0x1F8 is within ±256 (±22.5°) of self's yaw. Outcome: `sw 0x00000E01` to +0x4 → state=1, sub1=14, sub2=0, sub3=0. CRITICAL DELAY SLOT: `sw v0,4(s0)` @0x801017E4 is the delay slot of `j 0x80101a1c` @0x801017E0, so the store DOES execute and then the function returns immediately. (3) MISSING RUNTIME CONTEXT FOR +0x21A BITS 0x20/0x40: the claim calls them independent 'left/right side locks' but omits that they are assigned as a RANDOMIZED MUTUALLY-EXCLUSIVE PAIR elsewhere in the same overlay — 0x80102A20 'lhu v1,538(s1)' / 0x80102A24 'lbu v0,573(s1)' / 0x80102A28 'ori v1,v1,0x40' / 0x80102A2C 'andi v0,v0,0x2' / 0x80102A30 'beq v0,zero,0x80102A44' / 0x80102A34 'sh v1,538(s1)' (delay slot, always stores flags|0x40) / 0x80102A38 'andi v0,v1,0xffbf' / 0x80102A3C 'ori v0,v0,0x20' / 0x80102A40 'sh v0,538(s1)', with the whole randomiser gated by 0x801029A4 'lhu v0,538(s1)' / 0x801029AC 'andi v0,v0,0x60' / 0x801029B0 'bne v0,zero,0x80102A48' (runs only when NEITHER bit is set), and the source bit itself seeded by 0x80102A08 'jal 0x80015FE8' / 0x80102A0C 'sb v0,573(s1)'. The claim says block J "Falls through into block K." That is true, and block K writes a DIFFERENT state for the very same id-15 zombie, with no id gate:
  80101a04: lui v1,0x6            (3c 03 00 06)
  80101a0c: ori v1,v1,0x801       (34 63 08 01)   -> v1 = 0x00060801

findings.title: BLOCK K @0x801019E8 — the LAST writer, wins over everything: 0x00060801 + self+0x10E |= 0x4000
findings.meaning: Guards: player+0x156 (signed halfword) == -32768 EXACTLY (`bne` @0x801019F0 returns when it is anything else); s3 == 0 (player inside ±512); dist < 1000. Outcome: `sw 0x00060801` → +0x4 = 0x01 (state=1), +0x5 = 0x08 (sub1=8), +0x6 = 0x06 (sub2=6), +0x7 = 0x00; plus self+0x10E |= 0x4000. The headline "the LAST writer, wins over everything" is FALSE, and the "-32768 = HP sentinel" constant is an unproven inference sold as PROVEN.

(1) PRIMARY REFUTATION — a reachable path writes +0x4 and RETURNS without ever reaching block K:
  801017d8: bne v0,zero,0x801017e8
  801017dc: addiu v0,zero,3585        <- delay slot, ALWAYS executes (v0 = 0x0E01)
  801017e0: j 0x80101a1c              <- raw 08040687, target = EPILOGUE, NOT block K
  801017e4: sw v0,4(s0)               <- delay slot, raw ae020004 = sw v0,4(s0)
I scanned every branch/jump in 0x80101714..0x801019E4 for targets >= 0x80101A1C: exactly one exists, 0x801017E0. It jumps straight to the epilogue at 0x80101A1C (`lw ra,36(sp)` ... `jr ra` @0x80101A38), skipping block K's guards and its write entirely. So when the 0x801017B0/0x801017C4/0x801017D8 guard chain falls through, sub_state_1 = 0x0E is committed and block K NEVER RUNS. Block K does not "win over everything"; it only wins over the writers downstream of 0x801017E8.

(2) SECONDARY — "-32768 (0x8000) HP sentinel" is UNKNOWN, not proven. The claim proves +0x156 is HP (that part is correct), but never shows anything writes 0x8000 to it. I searched exhaustively for both ways to materialize 0x8000 in a register:
  - `addiu rX,zero,-32768`: only 3 sites in PSX.EXE (0x80053490, 0x80056F70, 0x8007B7EC) and 3 in EMZ0.BIN (0x801019EC, 0x8010220C, 0x8010B730) — none of the EXE ones stores to HP.
  - `ori rX,zero,0x8000`: 35 sites in PSX.EXE, ZERO in EMZ0.BIN — none feeding an HP store.
  The only -32768 store to a +0x156 field anywhere is `8010b730: addiu v1,zero,-32768` / `8010b738: sh v1,342(s2)`, and s2 there is `addu s2,a0,zero` @0x8010B46C — i.e. the ARGUMENT of a table-dispatched handler (0x8010B464 has no `jal`; only pointer-table refs at 0x8010CF3C/0x8010CF40). Whether a0 is the player or the zombie itself is UNRESOLVED, and being an EMZ0 state handler it is more likely self. I also scanned every overlay (STAGE1-7, EMOVL10_S0/S1, EMZ0, EMZ0_d1, OPENING, DIEDEMO, ...) for the absolute form `sh rt,-690(at)` after `lui at,0x800d`: the ONLY hit is MEM_CARD.BIN @0x80103B7C (savegame restore). No sentinel writer exists in any code I can reach.

(3) MINOR — the guard is not literally "s3 == 0". `801019f8: bne v0,zero` tests v0 from `801019f4: sll v0,s3,16`, i.e. only the LOW 16 BITS of s3. Equivalent in practice (returns are 0/+512/-512), but a literal port must mask to 16 bits.

(4) TOOL CAVEAT the claim inherited — re2_disasm.py annotates memory operands from the `lui` only, dropping the `addiu`. It prints `80040248: lhu v0,342(a2)  0x800d0156`, but a2 = 0x800CFBF8 (from `800401e0: addiu a2,a2,-1032`), so the real address is 0x800CFD4E. findings.meaning: The handler is a straight-line fall-through ladder with exactly ONE early exit. Every block except A writes +0x4 and keeps going, so LAST WRITER WINS. Precedence, highest first: (1) BLOCK A (0x0E01) — returns immediately via `j 0x80101a1c`, nothing else can run. findings.title: RNG FUN_80015FE8 — 8-bit return, state @0x800CE318; the two gates are exactly 1/4 and 1/2
findings.meaning: state = [0x800CE318]; hi = (state >> 7) & 0xFF; lo = (hi + state) & 0xFF; new_state = lo | (hi << 8); [0x800CE318] = new_state & 0xFFFF; return lo (8 bits). Block D's gate `andi v0,v0,0x3 / bne v0,zero,skip` passes only on lo & 3 == 0 → 1 in 4. Block E's `andi v0,v0,0x1 / bne v0,zero,skip` passes on lo & 1 == 0 → 1 in 2. For a byte-true port the generator itself must be replicated exactly (single shared 16-bit state, advanced once per call) — the number of calls per tick is part of the behaviour, and block D/E each consume one call ONLY when they reach it (i.e. after the distance, cone and global-mask gates pass).

findings.meaning: Low 7 bits are a countdown decremented once per player frame while nonzero; bit 0x80 is a latch. The zombie reads it two ways: block B and block J require the WHOLE byte == 0 (`bne v0,zero -> skip`), i.e. no cooldown AND no latch; block G requires only (byte & 0x80) == 0. When a side grab is committed the zombie SETS bit 0x80 on the player, which immediately locks out every other zombie's block G and both zombies' blocks B/J. This is the game's global 'only one zombie may have the player' arbiter and MUST be ported as shared state, not per-enemy state. The player-side code also sets bit 0x80 on lethal/near-lethal damage (0x800402D0, reached when hp < -14 or (player+0x154 & 0x1000)) and at 0x80020148 / 0x80021EB0 (which also write 0x800CFE10 = 5400 and 0x800CFE12 = 30).

verdict.why:
The CORE MECHANISM survives my re-disassembly — but the claim fails on three counts, one of which would produce a WRONG port. It is not "PROVEN" as delivered.

WHAT I INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED (all instructions re-dumped from EMZ0.BIN):

1. Decrement is real and the delay slot is handled correctly.
  80100470: lbu v0,574(s0)
  80100474: nop
  80100478: beq v0,zero,0x80100484
  8010047c: addiu v0,v0,-1        <- delay slot, ALWAYS executes
  80100480: sb v0,574(s0)
  When v0==0 the branch is taken and the store at 0x80100480 is skipped, so the -1 in the delay slot is dead. No underflow. Correct.
  Raw bytes verify: 0x80100470 = `3e 02 02 92` (lbu v0,0x23E(s0)), 0x80100480 = `3e 02 02 a2` (sb v0,0x23E(s0)).

2. It IS the per-frame prologue and s0 IS self — the claim asserted this without proof; I proved it. The containing function starts at 0x801002C0 (`addiu sp,sp,-40`; it is the only stack-alloc at or below 0x80100470 in the overlay) and 54 instructions after the decrement it dispatches the established state table:
  801004cc: lbu v0,4(s0)
  801004d8: lui at,0x8011
  801004dc: addu at,at,v0
  801004e0: lw v0,-14288(at)      -> 0x8010C830  (the zombie state table)
  801004e8: jalr v0
  801004ec: addu a0,s0,zero       <- delay slot: a0 = s0 = self
  Also 0x801004F8-0x80100508 increments a per-frame counter at +0x236. So s0=self and this is the per-tick root.
  CAVEAT the claim never mentions: 0x8010036C `bne v0,zero,0x80100640` (global AI-freeze gate on 0x800CFBDC & 0x20000000) jumps straight to the epilogue at 0x80100640, skipping the decrement AND the dispatch. The cooldown does NOT tick while globally frozen.

3. Reload of 60 is real and really is inside EXECUTOR[14]. Table dump: 0x8010C904 (= EXECUTOR base 0x8010C8CC + 14*4) -> 0x80104D74, and 0x8010C8C4 (DECISION[14]) -> 0x80104D6C which is just `jr ra / nop`. Function bounds proven, not assumed: prologue `addiu sp,sp,-32` at 0x80104D74, and 0x80104DAC `j 0x80104e30` proves 0x80104E30 is THIS function's epilogue. Raw bytes: 0x80104E28 = `3c 00 02 24` = addiu v0,zero,0x3C = 60; 0x80104E2C = `3e 02 02 a2` = sb v0,0x23E(s0); 0x80104E24 = `04 00 02 ae` = sw v0,4(s0).

4. The guards really do gate entry into sub1=14. All three cited sites are `lbu v0,574(s0)` + `bne v0,zero,<skip>`, and every block they skip ends in `addiu v0,zero,3585 / sw v0,4(s0)`. 3585 = 0x0E01, little-endian at +0x4 => +0x4=0x01 (state 1), +0x5=0x0E (sub1=14). WHY IT IS REFUTED:

(A) MATERIALLY INCOMPLETE READER SET — this breaks the port. I scanned the whole overlay for every load/store with immediate 0x0238..0x0244. There are SIX readers of +0x23E, not three. The claim lists only 0x8010179C, 0x801017E8, 0x801019B4 (all in DECISION[1] @0x80101714). It omits:
  80101ff8: lbu v0,574(s0) ... 80102004: bne v0,zero,0x80102098
  80102050: lbu v0,574(s0) ... 80102058: bne v0,zero,0x80102098
  801021d4: lbu v0,574(s0) ... 801021dc: bne v0,zero,0x80102208
These live in DECISION[2] (0x80101F7C) and gate the IDENTICAL transition — 0x80102090 `addiu v0,zero,3585` / 0x80102094 `sw v0,4(s0)`, and 0x80102200/0x80102204. The claim's summary "leaving only C/D/E/G/K able to fire" is therefore false as written — it is true only inside DECISION[1], and the claim never says so.

(B) A CITED CONSTANT IS NOT AT THE CITED ADDRESS. "ITS CONSTANTS: +0x23E (574) @0x8010179c" is wrong. At that address the instruction is:
  8010179c: bne v0,zero,0x80101830
which carries a branch offset, not 574. The `lbu v0,574(s0)` is at 0x80101790. (0x801017E8 and 0x801019B4 are correct.)

(C) "post-ATTACK" / "lunge" IS INFERRED BUT LABELED PROVEN. Nothing in the cited or surrounding code shows sub1=14 dealing damage. What executor[14] actually does: 0x80104DBC `sw v0,332(s0)` with v0=0x000F0011 (anim index 0x11, since FUN_8002959c reads it with `lbu v0,332(a0)`), and then only at anim frame +0x14D==10 (0x80104DD0-D8) it fires `jal 0x8001bf10` and `jal 0x8005bd6c` with a0=5. Proximity gates (<0x7D0 = 2000) plus a post-state lockout make "attack" a strong inference, but it is an inference, not a proof.

(D) Minor: the reload is not unconditional at the tail. It only fires when 0x80104E14 `jal 0x8002959c` returns nonzero (the anim-advance/completion path); if zero, 0x80104E1C `beq v0,zero,0x80104e30` jumps to the epilogue and neither the state word nor the cooldown is written. findings.meaning: Both writers set one of the two bits and clear the other (`ori 0x40` then, conditionally, `andi 0xffbf | ori 0x20`; and `ori 0x20` then, conditionally, `andi 0xffdf | ori 0x40`). findings.title: self+0x1F4 / +0x1F8 (block A's inputs) — a tagged distance and a REVERSE bearing to a tracked entity, both filled by the EXE
findings.meaning: +0x1F4 is a packed word: bits 0..29 hold sqrt(dx²+dz²) to a tracked entity (0x8008D2F4 again), bits 30 and 31 are two independent 'this slot is valid' tags OR'd in by two separate branches of the same EXE pass. +0x1F8 holds bearing(self -> that entity) + 2048 masked to 12 bits — i.e. the REVERSE direction (180° flipped). Block A therefore reads: 'some tagged entity is closer than 2000 AND I am facing within ±22.5° of the direction opposite to it' — that is why FUN_80015714 is used with the stored absolute angle instead of recomputing a bearing. Both fields are produced by the EXE before the AI dispatch, exactly like +0x1F0.
openQuestions: Which entity each of the two tag bits refers to (the EXE pass at 0x80065600.. reads candidates from sp+16 / sp+20 / sp+24 — three slots). Next xref: the prologue of the function containing 0x80065620 to see what fills those stack slots.

verdict.why:
THREE independent failures; the first is fatal to the stated meaning.

(1) DIRECTION INVERTED. FUN_800154AC returns the bearing of the vector (a2-a0, a3-a1) — the FIRST pair is the SOURCE. Byte-verified: 0x800154c8 = 0x00c48023 = "subu s0,a2,a0" (dx = X1-X0), and 0x800154dc "subu a0,a3,a1" (dz = Z1-Z0). The EXE call at 0x8006575c-0x8006576c passes a0/a1 = s5's position (SOURCE) and a2/a3 = the FIELD OWNER's position (TARGET):
  8006575c: lw a0,56(s5)
  80065760: lw a1,64(s5)
  80065764: lw a2,56(a3)
  80065768: lw a3,64(a3)
  8006576c: jal 0x800154ac
So it computes bearing(s5 -> owner), i.e. bearing(tracked_entity -> self), NOT bearing(self -> entity) as the claim asserts. The "addiu v0,v0,2048" at 0x8006579c therefore does NOT produce a reverse bearing — it CANCELS the backwards argument order, yielding bearing(owner -> s5) = the ordinary FORWARD bearing pointing AT the tracked entity.

The angle convention is proven by the already-established turn helper FUN_80015558, which computes bearing(self->target) and compares it to self+0x76 with NO offset, and applies +2048 ONLY on the negative-rate (flee) branch:
  80015584: lh a0,56(s1)        ; self.x -> SOURCE
  80015588: lh a1,64(s1)
  8001558c: jal 0x800154ac
  8001559c: bgez s0,0x800155b0  ; (=0x06010004) rate >= 0 -> SKIP the flip
  800155a0: sra v0,s0,16        ; delay slot
  800155a4: subu s2,zero,v0
  800155a8: addiu v0,v1,2048    ; reached ONLY when rate < 0
  800155b0: lhu a1,118(s1)      ; self facing +0x76
  800155b8: subu v0,v1,a1       ; compared DIRECTLY, no 180 offset
Confirmed a second time by FUN_80015614 (0x80015638 "lh a0,56(s0)" / 0x80015640 "jal 0x800154ac" / 0x80015648 "lhu v1,118(s0)" / 0x80015650 "subu v0,v0,v1"), which is the live-bearing twin of FUN_80015714 (0x80015714 "lhu v0,118(a0)" / 0x8001571c "subu a1,a1,v0"). Both test "is self facing within +/-window of the direction TOWARD the target". Therefore the cached angle at +0x1F8 must be the FORWARD direction, otherwise the two helpers would be mutually inconsistent.

Semantic cross-check: block A's outcome (0x801017dc "addiu v0,zero,3585" / 0x801017e4 "sw v0,4(s0)") is the SAME state word 3585 written by the parallel block at 0x80101828/0x8010182c, which gates on self+0x1F0 (0x801017fc "sltiu v0,s2,0x7d0", s2 loaded at 0x80101744 "lw s2,496(s0)") plus FUN_80015614 facing-toward-the-player. A block meaning "facing AWAY" cannot produce the same state as its facing-toward twin.

(2) TAG MODEL WRONG. There are THREE OR sites, not two, and they encode a 2-bit RANK, not two independent validity flags:
  80065788: lui v1,0x4000   -> 0x40000000 (nearest)
  800657e4: lui v1,0x8000   -> 0x80000000 (2nd nearest)
  80065840: lui v1,0xc000   -> 0xC0000000 (3rd nearest)  <-- missed entirely by the claim
This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: the overlay performs an EXACT-rank comparison that is meaningless under a "two independent tags" model:
  801002f8: lw v0,500(s0)
  801002fc: lui v1,0xc000
  80100300: and v0,v0,v1
  80100304: lui v1,0x4000
  80100308: bne v0,v1,0x80100320   ; an entity carrying BOTH bits FAILS this test

(3) QUOTE NOT FAITHFULLY COPIED. The claim's quoted blocks omit the instructions that load the store base register:
  80065798: lw v1,16(sp)   (omitted)
  800657f4: lw v1,20(sp)   (omitted)
As quoted, v1 still holds "lui v1,0x4000", so "sh v0,504(v1)" would store to 0x400001F8. The rules require instructions copied from tool output.

MINOR: s5 is not "the player". s5 = a0 of 0x80065518 (0x80065520 "addu s5,a0,zero"), passed through unchanged from 0x80060620/0x80060630, which is gated by 0x80060608 "lbu v1,8(a0)" == 69 (0x45) or 79 (0x4F). The player is a separate global [0x800CFE18] (0x80100314 "lw v0,-488(v0)"), one pointer before the scanned list at 0x800CFE1C (0x800655a8 "addiu s1,s7,15412", s7=0x800cc1e8 from 0x80065584).

WHAT SURVIVES: low 30 bits = integer sqrt(dx^2+dz^2) via 0x8008d2f4 (table-driven, LUT at 0x800adb8c via 0x8008d358 "lh t5,-9332(t5)"), written at 0x80065620 "sw s2,500(s0)"; confirmed by the reader's mask 0x801017b4 "lui v0,0x3fff" / 0x801017b8 "ori v0,v0,0xffff" / 0x801017bc "and v0,v1,v0". The <2000 threshold (0x801017c0 "sltiu v0,v0,0x7d0") and the +/-256 window (0x801017d4 "addiu a2,zero,256") are real. "EXE-written, overlay-read-only" is correct: a full scan of offsets 500/504 across PSX.EXE and all COMMON/BIN overlays shows EMZ0.BIN only ever loads them (0x801002f8, 0x801017a4, 0x801017cc, 0x8010200c, 0x80102034).

DELAY SLOTS re-checked and all correctly assigned in my analysis: 0x8006560c/0x80065610 (addu a0,a0,v1 completes the sum before the sqrt call); 0x800154e0/0x800154e4; 0x800154ec/0x800154f0; 0x80015530/0x80015534 (v0=4096 always executes); 0x8001559c/0x800155a0 (the decisive one — rate>=0 jumps past the +2048); 0x80015738/0x8001573c (returns 0 when within window); 0x801017b0/0x801017b4; 0x801017c4/0x801017c8; 0x801017d0/0x801017d4; 0x80060610/0x80060614; 0x80060670/0x80060674 (a0 untouched, passed through).
verdict.correction:
self+0x1F4 / +0x1F8 are a rank-tagged distance and a FORWARD bearing to a tracked type-0x45/0x4F entity, both filled by the EXE pass FUN_80065518 before the AI dispatch.

FUN_80065518(a0 = reference entity R) is called per frame with R = an entity whose type byte +0x8 is 0x45 or 0x4F (gate at 0x80060608 "lbu v1,8(a0)" / 0x80060610 "beq v1,v0(=69)" / 0x80060618 "bne v1,v0(=79)"), via the wrappers 0x80063bec and 0x80060650 (0x80060670 / 0x80063c0c "jal 0x80065518", a0 passed through unchanged).

It walks the entity-pointer list starting at 0x800CFE1C (0x800655a8 "addiu s1,s7,15412", s7 = 0x800cc1e8 set at 0x80065584), ending at [0x800CE334] (0x80065708 "lw v0,8524(s7)" / 0x80065710 "bne s1,v0,0x800655ac"). Note the player pointer sits at 0x800CFE18, one slot BEFORE the scanned range, and is the fallback used at 0x80100314.

Per candidate E (register s0) it:
  - gates on flags: 0x800655bc "andi v0,v0,0x1" / 0x800655c0 "beq v0,zero,0x80065704", and 0x800655d0 "andi v0,v0,0xc000" / 0x800655d4 "bne v0,zero,0x80065704"
  - computes dist = isqrt(dx^2 + dz^2) between E and R over +0x38/+0x40:
      800655dc: lw v0,56(s0) / 800655e0: lw v1,56(s5) / 800655e8: subu v0,v0,v1 / 800655ec: mult v0,v0
      800655f0: lw v0,64(s0) / 800655f4: lw v1,64(s5) / 800655f8: mflo a0 / 800655fc: subu v0,v0,v1
      80065604: mult v0,v0 / 80065608: mflo v1 / 8006560c: jal 0x8008d2f4 / 80065610: addu a0,a0,v1  [delay slot]
      80065618: addu s2,v0,zero
      80065620: sw s2,500(s0)        ; E->+0x1F4 = raw distance, tags CLEARED
  - runs an LOS/segment test (0x80065678 "jal 0x80050858" / 0x80065680 "bne v0,zero,0x80065704") and a +0x156 check (0x80065688 "lh v0,342(s0)" / 0x80065690 "bltz v0,0x80065704")
  - keeps a running 3-best sort in s6/s3/s4 with the winners in [sp+16]/[sp+20]/[sp+24].

After the loop it stamps the top three. +0x1F4 bits 30..31 are a 2-BIT RANK CODE, not two independent flags:
  rank 01 = 0x40000000 (nearest)      OR'd at 0x80065788-0x80065790
  rank 10 = 0x80000000 (second)       OR'd at 0x800657e4-0x800657ec
  rank 11 = 0xC0000000 (third)        OR'd at 0x80065840-0x80065848
  rank 00 = not in the top three
So +0x1F4 = (isqrt distance to R in bits 0..29) | (rank << 30).

+0x1F8 is the FORWARD bearing from the field owner toward R. For each of the three slots the EXE computes bearing(R -> E) — R is the SOURCE because FUN_800154AC subtracts the first pair from the second (0x800154c8 "subu s0,a2,a0", 0x800154dc "subu a0,a3,a1"):
  8006575c: lw a0,56(s5) / 80065760: lw a1,64(s5)      ; source = R
  80065764: lw a2,56(a3) / 80065768: lw a3,64(a3)      ; target = E
  8006576c: jal 0x800154ac / 80065770: nop             [delay slot]
  80065780: sh v0,0(a1)                                 ; cached at 0x800d4c70 / 0x800d4c72 / 0x800d4c74
  80065794: lhu v0,0(a1)
  80065798: lw v1,16(sp)                                ; v1 = E  (the base register)
  8006579c: addiu v0,v0,2048
  800657a0: andi v0,v0,0xfff
  800657a4: sh v0,504(v1)                               ; E->+0x1F8
The +2048 does NOT create a reverse bearing: it undoes the source/target order, so the stored value is bearing(E -> R), the direction pointing straight AT R. Angle space: 0 = +X, 1024 = -Z, 2048 = -X, 3072 = +Z (from FUN_800154AC's 0x800154b0 "addiu v0,zero,1024", 0x800154e8 "addiu v0,zero,3072", 0x80015534 "addiu v0,zero,4096", 0x80015538 "addiu v0,zero,2048", 0x8001553c "subu v0,v0,v1"), identical to the entity facing field +0x76.

Consequently BLOCK A @0x801017a4 reads: "I am ranked in the top three around R (any rank), AND R is closer than 2000, AND I am facing within +/-22.5 degrees TOWARD R":
  801017a0: lui v0,0xc000        [delay slot of the 0x8010179c bne]
  801017a4: lw v1,500(s0)
  801017ac: and v0,v1,v0         ; rank != 0 ?
  801017b0: beq v0,zero,0x801017e8
  801017b4: lui v0,0x3fff        [delay slot]
  801017b8: ori v0,v0,0xffff
  801017bc: and v0,v1,v0         ; strip rank -> distance
  801017c0: sltiu v0,v0,0x7d0    ; < 2000
  801017c4: beq v0,zero,0x801017e8
  801017c8: addu a0,s0,zero      [delay slot]
  801017cc: lh a1,504(s0)        ; cached FORWARD bearing to R
  801017d0: jal 0x80015714
  801017d4: addiu a2,zero,256    [delay slot]  +/-256 of 4096 = +/-22.5 deg
  801017d8: bne v0,zero,0x801017e8
  801017dc: addiu v0,zero,3585   [delay slot]
  801017e0: j 0x80101a1c
  801017e4: sw v0,4(s0)          ; state = 3585 (0xE01)
FUN_80015714 is used with the cached angle purely to avoid recomputing the bearing — it is the pre-computed twin of FUN_80015614 (0x80015638 "lh a0,56(s0)" ... 0x80015650 "subu v0,v0,v1"), which does the identical facing-TOWARD test from live coordinates. Block B immediately after (0x801017f8 "bne v0,zero,0x80101830" on the FUN_80015614 result with window 1300, 0x801017fc "sltiu v0,s2,0x7d0" on +0x1F0) writes the SAME state 3585 at 0x8010182c — the two blocks are the player-facing and R-facing variants of one rule.

A second overlay site distinguishes a SPECIFIC rank and therefore must be ported with the 2-bit encoding, not booleans:
  801002f8: lw v0,500(s0) / 801002fc: lui v1,0xc000 / 80100300: and v0,v0,v1
  80100304: lui v1,0x4000 / 80100308: bne v0,v1,0x80100320
  80100310: lui v0,0x800d / 80100314: lw v0,-488(v0)   ; [0x800CFE18] = player
  8010231c: addiu s1,v0,56
i.e. "only if I am the SINGLE nearest (rank 01) do I retarget to the player's coordinates".

UNKNOWN / not established here: the concrete identity of entity types 0x45 and 0x4F; the exact meaning of the +0x156 sign gate at 0x80065688 and of FUN_80050858; whether +0x1F4 is ever cleared for entities that fail the early flag gates at 0x800655c0 / 0x800655d4 (those keep last frame's value, since the clearing store 0x80065620 is downstream of both) — the two "sw zero,500(s0)" sites at 0x80057418 and 0x80057aac were not traced.

verdict.why:
The load-bearing PROVEN part survives, but two INFERRED sub-claims are contradicted by the instructions.

=== WHAT I INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED ===
Polarity is exactly as claimed. Both compare sites are byte-identical (`06 01 03 92 06 01 22 92` at BOTH 0x80101808 and 0x80101914) = `lbu v1,262(s0)` / `lbu v0,262(s1)`.
  80101814: 06 00 62 10  -> 0x10620006 = beq v1,v0,0x80101830 ; delay slot 80101818 = nop
  80101920: 31 00 62 14  -> 0x14620031 = bne v1,v0,0x801019e8 ; delay slot 80101924 = nop
Both delay slots are nop, so no logic inversion. Block B body (0x8010181c-0x8010182c) requires DIFFER; block G body (0x80101928+) requires MATCH. CONFIRMED.
Operands confirmed too: s0 = self (`addu s0,a0,zero` @0x8010171c); s1 = player (`lui s1,0x800d` @0x80101794 + `addiu s1,s1,-1032` @0x80101798 = 0x800CFBF8). That independently validates 0x800CFBF8+0x106 = 0x800CFCFE, so "0x800CFCFE = player+0x106" is right.

=== REFUTATION 1: "copied enemy<-player at 0x8001AF30" is FALSE ===
s1 there is NOT the player. Function head is 0x8001ad3c. The source is found by a list walk keyed on byte +0x8:
  8001ad60: andi a0,a0,0xff              ; caller passes a class byte
  8001ad80: lbu v0,8(s0)
  8001ad88: bne v0,a0,0x8001ada4         ; skip entities whose +0x8 != a0
  8001ad9c: beq v0,zero,0x8001b1cc
  8001ada0: addu s1,s0,zero              ; DELAY SLOT -> s1 = the MATCHED entity, unconditionally
And the destination copies that same key byte back:
  8001af10: lbu v0,8(s1)
  8001af18: sb v0,8(s0)
So source and destination agree on +0x8 by construction: this is "clone an existing entity of class N into a freshly allocated 584-byte slot" (size from `addiu s2,s0,584` @0x8001ae34), never player->enemy. The player struct 0x800CFBF8 is a fixed global, not an element of the walked list at 0x800D3C2C (`addiu a1,s3,15404` @0x8001ad5c). The parenthetical "a freshly spawned enemy starts on the player's value" is an invention.

=== REFUTATION 2: "subtracting a shifted height term from a base" is FALSE ===
In `subu a0,a0,v1` @0x80036970, a0 is NOT a base. a0 is built by:
  8003693c: sll a0,v0,16
  80036950: sra a0,a0,31                 ; sign-bit replication -> 0 or -1
That is the rounding correction of a compiler signed-division idiom spanning 0x80036934-0x80036974:
  80036934: lui a1,0x91a2
  80036938: ori a1,a1,0xb3c5             ; magic 0x91A2B3C5
  80036944: mult v1,a1
  80036964: mfhi t0
  80036968: addu v1,t0,v1
  8003696c: sra v1,v1,10                 ; the DIVISION shift, not a "shifted height"
Exhaustive evaluation over n = -40000..40000 gives exactly f(n) = -(n / 1800), C truncation: f(1799)=0, f(1800)=-1, f(3600)=-2, f(-1800)=+1 — breakpoints on every multiple of 1800. There is no base and no height shift.

=== UNKNOWN (claim overstates) ===
The dividend n is the return of the call at 0x8003692c (`jal 0x8004fba0`, a0=self+0x84, a1=450, a2=16384). I did not trace that return, so calling it "a height" is unproven. Whose struct s0 is in that EXE routine is also unproven.

verdict.why:
The read side is correct, but the claim's central negative assertion is factually FALSE, and its writer enumeration is incomplete.

=== FATAL: "No writer of self+0x110 bit 0 was located at all" is REFUTED ===
FUN_8003567c writes self+0x110 twice, and the ZOMBIE OVERLAY ITSELF calls it:

  80100634: addu a0,s0,zero          ; a0 = self
  80100638: jal 0x8003567c
  8010063c: addiu a1,zero,1024       ; DELAY SLOT -> a1 = 0x400

Inside FUN_8003567c (s0 = a0 = the entity, proven @0x80035684 `addu s0,a0,zero`):

  80035698: bne v0,zero,0x800356ec
  8003569c: sw zero,272(s0)          ; DELAY SLOT -> self+0x110 = 0 ALWAYS (both paths)
  ...
  800356c8: lbu a2,262(s0)           ; +0x106 (same field the overlay reads @0x8010180c)
  800356cc: lhu a1,144(s0)           ; +0x90
  800356d0: jal 0x8004c1bc
  800356d4: sllv a2,v0,a2            ; DELAY SLOT -> a2 = 1 << self[+0x106]
  800356d8: sw v0,272(s0)            ; self+0x110 = return value of FUN_8004c1bc

Byte-verified: 0x8003569c = `10 01 00 ae` = 0xae000110 (op 0x2b SW, rs=s0, imm=272);
0x800356d8 = `10 01 02 ae` = 0xae020110 (op 0x2b SW, rs=s0, rt=v0, imm=272);
0x800356d0 = `6f 30 01 0c` = jal 0x8004c1bc. So +0x110 is a per-frame word produced by
FUN_8004c1bc and consumed next frame by `lw v0,272(s0)` @0x80101844. The writer was
findable by a plain offset-272 store scan; the claim simply did not run one.

=== INCOMPLETE: "the only writers of +0x1D4 found" ===
An exhaustive scan of PSX.EXE + EMZ0.BIN for offset-468 accesses returns 9 lbu-table
arms, not the 4 claimed. Missing: 0x80056d04, 0x80056d20, 0x80056d3c, 0x80056d58,

= 0x800a79e9. Also missing four zero-stores: 0x80056ba4, 0x80056dcc, 0x800573e8,
0x80057a7c (all `sh zero,468(...)`).
(Two further scan hits, `8001b53c: sw v0,468(at)` = 0x800d01d4 and
`80080d90: sh v0,468(v1)` = 0x800b01d4, are ABSOLUTE globals, not self+0x1D4 — correctly
excluded, but only by luck since the claim never scanned.)

=== DELAY SLOTS OMITTED FROM THE QUOTED LISTING ===
The claim's listing jumps 8010183c -> 80101844 and ends at 80101850, dropping two
NON-nop, load-bearing delay slots:
  80101840: sltiu v0,s2,0xdac   ; executes ALWAYS; clobbers v0 AND computes the
                                ; dist<3500 predicate consumed at 0x80101860
  80101854: addiu v0,zero,2561  ; executes ALWAYS; this IS the value stored by
                                ; 80101858: sw v0,4(s0)
Byte-verified: 0x80101854 = `01 0a 02 24` = 0x24020a01 (ADDIU v0,zero,0x0a01). By
omitting it the claim never states what the gate DOES (set self+0x4 = 0xA01).

=== UNDER-CLAIMED: +0x1D4's structure IS provable from the same overlay ===
Marking the field wholly UNKNOWN is too pessimistic; EMZ0 itself shows it is packed:
  8010424c: lhu a1,468(s1)
  80104250: addiu a2,zero,32
  80104254: jal 0x80015714
  80104258: andi a1,a1,0xfff      ; DELAY SLOT -> low 12 bits = an ANGLE, fed to the
                                  ; turn helper 0x80015714 at rate 32
  80104214: andi a0,a0,0x4000     ; a single top bit tested as a flag
That the low 12 bits are a 4096-unit angle and the top bits are flags is PROVED by these
instructions; it also explains cleanly why the lbu writers (values 0..255) never reach
0xC000.
